correctness.rationale: Positive-coefficient Q(z)/(1-H(z)) has a unique strictly dominant simple pole by adjacent exponents; its exact residue and bivariate implicit pole derivatives yield fixed-index coefficient and count formulas. The classical eta modular identity gives log Q=A/t+0.5 log(t/2pi)+small, E=A/t^2-1/(2t)+small and V=2A/t^3-1/(2t^2)+small. Root monotonicity then proves sqrt(j)t->s_gamma and the explicit Theta and Xi values; Taylor expansion at sqrt(A/j) establishes the log-j correction and j^-9/8 amplitude. The public standard-library verifier passed 975 exact coefficient comparisons, 36 numerical phase checks, and eight asymptotic comparisons; finite checks are supplementary and cannot establish the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: Originality assessed for the coupled variable-monomial-index phase theorem, not for the already classical fixed-j supercritical pole/Gaussian implications. Published motivating 2024 paper conjectures fixed-j exponential growth but contains no j-dependent crossover; a general 2004 supercritical-sequences theorem subsumes the elementary fixed-j results, but no examined source supplies the critical weight, duality, scaled variance, or explicit refined large-j amplitude. Multiple mathematical-record semantic queries and prior-claim comparisons returned no matching theorem; residual possibility of a stronger general variable-parameter transfer result is acknowledged.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently parameterized analytic-combinatorics result could already give the large-index phase laws.
The fixed-parameter pole and Gaussian results are prior theory and are not claimed original.
No independent mathematician has audited the results or confirmed publication priority.

value.rationale: The motivator is a concrete 2024 reciprocal generating-function conjecture. Rather than a routine fixed-j corollary, the varied monomial degree and exponentially sqrt(j)-scaled marker weight reveal a nontrivial, sharp phase profile with exactly self-dual marked/unmarked mass, a symmetric fluctuation law with a unique maximum, and a quantitative logarithmic correction plus coefficient amplitude. These identify a natural quantitative transition in partition-block composition sizes and a precise asymptotic regime absent from the motivating formulas; the result deliberately makes no uniform simultaneous-n-j claim.
